name: Kaziranga National Park
ecosystem: Brahmaputra floodplain grassland and wetland
summary: A globally important floodplain landscape known for its large population of the greater one-horned rhinoceros.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
ecosystem: Shivalik foothills, sal forest and riverine habitat
summary: India's oldest national park and a core component of the Corbett Tiger Reserve landscape.

name: Gir National Park
ecosystem: Dry deciduous forest and scrub
summary: The last natural stronghold of the Asiatic lion.

name: Kanha National Park
ecosystem: Sal forest, meadows and bamboo woodland
summary: Known for its hard-ground barasingha recovery and extensive central Indian forest landscape.

name: Sundarbans National Park
ecosystem: Tidal mangrove forest and estuary
summary: Part of the world's largest mangrove forest complex and a UNESCO World Heritage property.

name: Hemis National Park
ecosystem: Trans-Himalayan cold desert and alpine steppe
summary: A high-altitude protected landscape famous for snow leopard habitat.

name: Great Himalayan National Park
ecosystem: Western Himalayan temperate and alpine ecosystems
summary: A UNESCO-listed mountain conservation landscape spanning a range of Himalayan habitats.

name: Periyar National Park
ecosystem: Western Ghats evergreen forest and reservoir
summary: A major Western Ghats forest landscape centred around the Periyar lake and reservoir.

name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary
ecosystem: Alluvial grassland and wetland
summary: A compact Brahmaputra floodplain sanctuary with a notable density of one-horned rhinoceros.

name: Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary
ecosystem: Northern Western Ghats semi-evergreen forest
summary: A Western Ghats sanctuary important for the Indian giant squirrel and forest biodiversity.

name: Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary
ecosystem: Terai grassland, riverine forest and wetlands
summary: A Terai landscape along the Girwa and other river systems, supporting rare aquatic and terrestrial wildlife.

name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
ecosystem: Riverine islands and wetland
summary: A cluster of river islands on the Cauvery, known for nesting waterbirds.

name: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary
ecosystem: Freshwater irrigation tank and wetland
summary: One of India's best-known historic bird sanctuaries, centred on a seasonal tank.

name: Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary
ecosystem: Shallow freshwater lake and marsh
summary: A large seasonal wetland and important wintering ground for migratory waterbirds.

name: Asan Conservation Reserve
ecosystem: Riverine wetland and reservoir
summary: India's first Ramsar site in the conservation-reserve category; an important bird habitat.

name: Aghanashini Lion-tailed Macaque Conservation Reserve
ecosystem: Western Ghats evergreen and semi-evergreen forest
summary: A large Western Ghats conservation landscape created to protect threatened rainforest biodiversity.

name: Keshopur-Miani Community Reserve
ecosystem: Marsh, seasonal ponds and agricultural wetland mosaic
summary: A community-managed wetland conservation area and Ramsar site.

name: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
ecosystem: Western Ghats mosaic: evergreen, moist deciduous, shola and grassland
summary: India's first biosphere reserve, connecting several important protected areas across three states.

name: Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve
ecosystem: Satpura highlands, sal and teak forest
summary: A central Indian highland landscape containing Satpura National Park and adjoining conservation areas.

name: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve
ecosystem: Dry deciduous teak forest, bamboo and lakes
summary: A prominent central Indian tiger landscape with dry deciduous forest and water bodies.

name: Pench Tiger Reserve
ecosystem: Teak forest, dry deciduous woodland and riverine habitat
summary: A transboundary tiger landscape spanning Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

name: Mysore Elephant Reserve
ecosystem: Southern Western Ghats and connected forest corridors
summary: An important elephant landscape linking forest habitats in southern Karnataka.

name: Chilika Lake
ecosystem: Brackish-water lagoon, mudflats and islands
summary: A major brackish lagoon and internationally important wetland supporting fisheries and migratory birds.

name: Loktak Lake
ecosystem: Freshwater lake with floating phumdis
summary: Northeast India's largest freshwater lake, closely associated with floating phumdi wetlands and Keibul Lamjao.

name: East Kolkata Wetlands
ecosystem: Urban sewage-fed wetlands and aquaculture ponds
summary: A globally recognised urban wetland system that supports wastewater treatment, aquaculture and livelihoods.

name: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
ecosystem: Coral reefs, seagrass beds and islands
summary: A chain of islands and shallow marine habitats with coral reefs and seagrass meadows.

name: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
ecosystem: Tropical island, coral reef and seagrass habitat
summary: A marine protected landscape around islands off the South Andaman coast.

name: Western Ghats
state: Maharashtra / Goa / Karnataka / Kerala / Tamil Nadu
ecosystem: Tropical montane, evergreen forest, shola and grassland
summary: A serial World Heritage property recognised for exceptional biodiversity and endemism.

name: Khangchendzonga National Park
ecosystem: Eastern Himalayan alpine, subalpine and glacial ecosystems
summary: India's first mixed World Heritage property, recognised for natural and cultural values.

name: Ameenpur Lake
ecosystem: Urban freshwater lake and rocky outcrops
summary: Recognised as a Biodiversity Heritage Site and noted for its urban wetland biodiversity.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Grove
ecosystem: Subtropical broadleaf sacred forest
summary: A community-protected sacred forest demonstrating traditional conservation practices.

name: Banni Grasslands
ecosystem: Arid and semi-arid grassland and seasonal wetlands
summary: One of India's largest natural grassland systems, shaped by arid climate and pastoral use.

name: Pichavaram Mangroves
ecosystem: Tidal mangrove forest and estuary
summary: A well-known mangrove ecosystem with tidal creeks and islands.

name: Chandratal Wetland
ecosystem: High-altitude freshwater lake and alpine meadow
summary: A high-altitude Himalayan wetland in a cold desert landscape.

name: Trans-Himalaya
ecosystem: Cold desert, alpine steppe and high-altitude wetlands
summary: A high-altitude biogeographic zone characterised by cold deserts, steppe and sparse alpine vegetation.

name: Western Ghats
state: Maharashtra / Goa / Karnataka / Kerala / Tamil Nadu
ecosystem: Tropical evergreen, moist deciduous, shola and montane grassland
summary: A global biodiversity hotspot with high levels of endemism and major river catchments.
